content.text:
Universal Agent Memory is a compatible, deterministic external-agent baseline built around a repository-local, file-backed handoff workflow—not unverified IDE hooks or an API-dependent service.

- Binary: `entire-agent-universal-memory`, protocol v1.
- Workflow: `capture` persists bounded/redacted coding context; `handoff` reads the selected session for the deployment agent.
- Storage: `<repo>/.entire/universal-memory/sessions/<session-id>.jsonl`, created only under the supplied repository and never committed.
- Transcript: JSONL records with role, content, timestamp, plus optional modified-file metadata. Token accounting is intentionally unavailable.
- Protocol baseline: implements static metadata/detection, safe session read/write, Base64 transcript chunking/reassembly, and an explicit `universal-memory handoff` resume command.
- Initial capabilities are deliberately minimal: hooks, transcript analysis/preparation, token calculation, text generation, hook-response writing, and subagent extraction are all disabled.
- Safety: handoffs are size-limited; obvious credentials are redacted; missing context returns an explicit result rather than inventing history.
- Native IDE hook support is explicitly unverified and deferred until real payloads are captured. Deterministic tests do not need a native IDE; interactive lifecycle tests currently require an agent CLI and `tmux` on the Windows host.
